headline: Town boards advanced elementary school designs, examined multi-million-dollar capital needs, and scheduled special hearings on the proposed Route 9 Costco.
synopsis: Southborough boards focused heavily on long-range school planning, fiscal projections, and commercial development during the week. The Elementary School Building Committee voted to advance Option 3 into schematic design, while the Capital Improvement and Planning Committee evaluated up to $49 million in bondable requests dominated by the Neary School project. The Board of Health adopted FY28 budget scenarios, warning that Friday office closures and septic review delays would occur if an operating override fails. Meanwhile, the Planning Board extended its review timeline and set a special November meeting for the Costco proposal, and the Select Board advanced legislation to make the Town Clerk an appointed position.

highlights.title: Option 3 advanced to schematic design for elementary school project
highlights.why: The committee voted 4-0 to direct Tappé Architects to develop detailed schematic designs and site cost estimates for Option 3, while noting other options remain under evaluation.

highlights.title: FY28 capital plan reviewed, including $45 million school placeholder
highlights.why: The committee examined departmental capital requests totaling $2.15 million in appropriations and up to $49 million in bondable debt, led by a $45 million placeholder for the Neary School.

highlights.title: Board of Health outlines service cutbacks under level-funded budget
highlights.why: The board approved its FY28 requests and warned that failing to pass an operating override would trigger Friday office closures, septic review backlogs, and potential cuts to town flu clinics.

highlights.title: Planning Board schedules special meeting and extends Costco deadline
highlights.why: With traffic peer reviews still pending, the board set a special November 2 meeting for the 21 Coslin Drive Costco proposal and extended the statutory decision deadline to December 18, 2026.

highlights.title: Select Board advances petition to make Town Clerk appointed
highlights.why: The board voted unanimously to send a home rule petition to state legislators to implement Town Meeting's decision transitioning the Town Clerk from an elected office to an appointed position.

highlights.title: Zoning bylaw amendments drafted to match state Chapter 40A rules
highlights.why: The board reviewed draft amendments aligning local zoning with state law regarding nonconforming lots, four-year abandonment rules, and practical difficulty variance criteria for the 2027 Town Meeting.
